model.doc:
Uniformly charged sphere in an unbounded uniform dielectric (Poisson only).

    Axisymmetric (r, z) model, no ions and no flow:
      -lap phi = q for rho < R, 0 outside, with rho = sqrt(r^2 + z^2), delta = 1.
    Exact solution (phi -> 0 at infinity):
      phi = q R^2/2 - q rho^2/6 inside,  phi = q R^3 / (3 rho) outside.
    The mesh follows the sphere surface, so the source jumps exactly on
    element edges.  The axis r = 0 is a symmetry line (natural BC).

param_info.q: uniform charge density: -lap phi = q inside, 0 outside
param_info.h_sphere: element size at the sphere surface (0 = R/20)
param_info.outer_bc: 1: Robin far field dphi/dn = -phi/R_out (exact for a monopole), 0: Dirichlet with the exact value

checks.note: all mesh checks pass (details: mesh_checks, mesh/diagnose.json)

notes: Axisymmetric (r, z): mesh x = r >= 0, y = z; the UI may mirror about r = 0.
Integrals in summary.json are per radian (r dr dz, r ds) unless named *_3d; *_3d = 2 pi * per radian.
outer BC: Robin dphi/dn = -phi/R_out; h_sphere = 0.05, h_far = 0.5.

mesh_views.title: Whole domain, boundaries coloured by physical group
mesh_views.what_to_check: every boundary has the expected colour and name (red dots = unnamed edges); the domain has the intended shape and size; the element density is highest at charged/reacting walls

mesh_views.title: Zoom on the finest region, around boundary 'axis' (smallest h), elements coloured by shape quality q (1 = equilateral)
mesh_views.what_to_check: the layer of small elements hugs the wall; size grows smoothly away from it with no sudden jumps; no dark (low-q) slivers; curved P2 edges follow the wall arc
